dbtQuestions: What worked well for you today in terms of self-care?
When you felt a strong urge, what strategy did you use (or could have used)?
What emotions did you notice before using? And after?
What would help you feel safer in the coming days?
Looking at today, what small change would you make tomorrow?
What were your triggers today? How could you prepare for them?
What need were you trying to meet with the use?
If a friend were in the same situation, what would you tell them?
What brings you joy or peace, beyond using?
How can you be kind to yourself tomorrow?
How can you take care of yourself today?
What conscious choice did you make today?
How can you honor your body today?
What have you learned about yourself recently?
What small step did you take this week?
What makes you feel grateful today?
What part of your day went better than expected?
How are you feeling right now, without judgment?
What person or thing supported you today?
What could you do tomorrow to feel more connected to yourself?
What physical sensation did you notice today that deserves attention?
How is your energy level? What does it need?
What repetitive thought did you have today? Is it helpful or harmful?
What would you do if you had more energy today?
What moment from today would you like to repeat?
How could you make your space more comfortable tomorrow?
What person came to mind today? Why do you think that was?
If you could give advice to 'yesterday's you', what would it be?
What stops you from asking for help when you need it?
What small victory did you have today that deserves recognition?
reflectiveQuestions: Each day is a new opportunity to take care of yourself.
Your journey is unique. There is no right or wrong timeline.
Harm reduction is about progress, not perfection.
You are stronger than you think, even on difficult days.
Taking care of yourself is not selfishness, it's survival.
Small changes create big transformations.
Your worth does not depend on yesterday's choices.
Today is a good day to be kind to yourself.
Recovery is not linear, and that's okay.
You deserve compassion, especially from yourself.
Every conscious breath is an act of courage.
You don't have to do this alone. Support exists.
Your body is always on your side, even when it doesn't seem like it.
Allowing yourself to rest is also productive.
Relapses are information, not failures.
You're doing the best you can with what you have now.
Change begins with acceptance, not judgment.
Your feelings are valid, all of them.
Seeking help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
Today you can choose a different path, even a small one.
Your story doesn't end here.
You are worthy of love and care, unconditionally.
Every moment is an opportunity to start again.
Self-care doesn't have to be perfect to be valid.
You are learning, and that's already incredible.

Solidão: Send a message to a friend
Tristeza: Allow yourself to cry without judgment

Stress: 4-7-8 breathing: inhale 4s, hold 7s, exhale 8s. Repeat 4x when you feel tension rising
STOP technique: Stop, Take a breath, Observe (what you feel), Proceed (with conscious choice)
Write 3 things you can control right now (e.g. drink water, step out 5min, let someone know)
Ansiedade: 5-4-3-2-1: Name 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch, 2 you smell, 1 you taste
Ice on hands or face for 30s: intense sensation brings you to the present (DBT skill - TIP)
Challenge the thought: 'Is it fact or interpretation? What's the real probability? What would I tell a friend?'
Solidão: Message 3 people (no expectation of immediate reply): share something neutral, create connection
Leave the house for 15min: café, walk, library. Presence of others helps even without interaction
Online activity with people (discord, gaming, livestream): connection counts, even virtual
Festa: Set a limit BEFOREHAND: max X uses, departure time, budget. Tell someone your plan
Alternate: 1 drink → 1 water/juice. Keep a cup in hand (less social pressure to drink)
Identify a trusted person nearby + planned transport back + safe place if you need to leave
Trabalho: Micro-breaks: every 25min take 5min (wash face, stretch, snack). Prevents accumulated burnout
Prioritize max 3 tasks/day: rest is a bonus. Unrealistic pressure is a trigger for use
If overwhelmed: email/message your manager 'I need a deadline/workload adjustment'. Asking for help ≠ weakness
Família: Clear boundaries: 'I can't talk about X right now' or 'I need space, I'll talk to you tomorrow'
Self-compassion: 'I'm doing the best I can with what I have now'. Guilt doesn't help
Support network outside family: friend, therapist, online group. Don't rely only on those who trigger you
Hábito: Break the pattern: change 1 step of the routine (different route, different time, different context)
Substitute: special tea/coffee, cold shower, 10 push-ups, 5min of a game. Keeps hands + mind occupied
Delay 15min: 'I can do this in 15min if I still want to'. Often the urge passes
Tristeza: Validate the emotion: 'It makes sense to feel this'. Sadness is not weakness, it's information about what matters
Radical self-care: warm bath, a meal you like, clean clothes. Body affects mind
Talk to someone (friend, family, therapist): sharing relieves, you don't have to solve it alone
Dependência: HALT check: am I Hungry? Angry? Lonely? Tired? Resolve the real need first
Surf the urge: imagine it as a wave - rises, peaks (3-15min), falls. I don't have to act at the peak
If I'm going to use: plan harm reduction (smaller dose, safe context, someone knows where I am, water/food ready)

bedtimeConsist.msgVeryConsistent: 🎯 You go to bed at very similar times (variation <30min). Excellent! Your body learns to prepare for sleep at the same time, improving sleep quality and making it easier to fall asleep.
bedtimeConsist.msgConsistent: ⚖️ Moderate variation (±{{val}}h in bedtime). Some consistency, but you can improve. Try to set a 30-min window (e.g. 11pm-11:30pm) for bedtime, even on weekends.
bedtimeConsist.msgVariable: 🌪️ Very variable bedtimes (±{{val}}h difference). This confuses the circadian rhythm — the body doesn't know when to prepare for sleep. Result: harder to fall asleep, less deep sleep. Starting by reducing to ±1h already helps.

educationalResources.title: What is Harm Reduction?
educationalResources.content: HR is a set of practical strategies to minimize risks of drug use, without requiring abstinence.

educationalResources.title: Hydration & Rest
educationalResources.content: Stimulants dehydrate. Drink water regularly. Sleep is essential for recovery.

educationalResources.title: Interval Between Uses
educationalResources.content: Spacing reduces tolerance and body harm. Ideally >2h between doses.

educationalResources.title: Substance Testing
educationalResources.content: Whenever possible, test before using. CheckIn (Lisbon), MAPS (Porto).

educationalResources.title: Warning Signs
educationalResources.content: Chest pain, confusion, high temperature = emergency (112).

educationalResources.title: Tolerance & Breaks
educationalResources.content: The body adapts. Breaks help reduce tolerance.
